scope: Freeze the matched FT6 evaluation panel and execute the three feedback policies across five history regimes, six held-out demands and six changed demands using exact candidate ties and real paid chosen executions. Add history-removal and feedback-off causal controls and a fixed-bias comparator. This sub-batch records the full grid and counterexamples; FT6.3b independently audits the frozen result and applies the common FT6 stabilization/release gate.

source_contract.continuation_plan: Full Theory Engine Batched Plan revision 1.1, FT6.3 and FT6 gate
source_contract.accepted_predecessor: FT6.2 tie-only feedback, actual paid choice binding and measured n-pair episodes accepted
source_contract.unchanged_boundaries: TIM, seat dimensionality, native semantic law, grade-v1 wallet law, load-v1 reserve, certificate scope and H.retained remain unchanged

fixed_factorial.construction: Each of 15 policy/history cells receives the same ordered six held-out then six changed demand IDs. Demand fixtures and both alternatives are fixed before history is applied. Every alternative is preflighted on an exact isolated native clone; the chosen alternative is executed on its paired clone and must bind to its prospective paid element multiset.
fixed_factorial.matching: Within each demand, alternatives are equally eligible and tied on TD5 priority, exact estimated native time and exact extra energy. Only feedback score or, when inactive/tied, stable identity may differ. Fixtures do not inspect target answers, realized success or desired occupancy when constructing candidates.
fixed_factorial.boundedness: At most two exact alternatives per demand, twelve demands per cell and fifteen primary cells. Raw event detail is saved privately; the repository retains scenario identities, hashes, aggregate results and exact evidence hashes.

history_regimes.independent-use: Six completed paid training episodes classified independent. Their exact element deltas create the only nonzero conditioning score under non-null policies.
history_regimes.no-use: Same native baseline and elapsed history turns, with no post-baseline paid use and all scores zero.
history_regimes.supported-use: The same paid element deltas as independent-use, classified supported; no independent credit.
history_regimes.failed-use: The same completed paid element deltas occur inside attempts with failed outcomes and are classified failed; no independent credit or success claim.
history_regimes.fixed-bias: History scores are removed and feedback is disabled. A prospectively fixed stable-identity order favors the same initial alternative as the trained condition. It is an external comparator, never relabeled as conditioning.

causal_controls.history_removal: For every independent-use non-null row, replace the ledger with an exact same-actor, same-TIM zero-score ledger at the evaluation boundary; do not change candidates, native fixture or stable identities.
causal_controls.feedback_off: For every independent-use non-null row, retain the exact trained ledger but call the accepted chooser with feedback=false; do not change candidates or native fixture.
causal_controls.expected_discrimination: A claimed conditioning effect requires the trained choice to differ from both controls in at least one held-out demand and the chosen request's actual paid completion to match its declared elements. Fixed bias must remain distinguishable by its lack of score dependence and changed-condition response.
causal_controls.failure_policy: Unsupported, failed and no-use histories must not mint independent score. Null policy must remain behaviorally identical to feedback-off for the same candidates. All counterexamples remain in the grid.

stabilization_measurement.training: The latest six completed paid n training episodes are evaluated by the accepted unique four-of-six measured occupancy rule.
stabilization_measurement.held_out: A stabilization candidate requires the same unique DCNH n-pair in at least four of the six held-out completed compensation episodes. Non-n choices, incomplete work and ties cannot be counted as occupancy evidence.
stabilization_measurement.changed: The six changed demands measure persistence or shift but do not retroactively alter the held-out criterion. success-decay-v1 receives exactly four declared idle turns for affected elements before C4; success-v1 and null receive the same turn schedule without score decay.
stabilization_measurement.boundary: FT6.3a reports candidate stabilization only. It never applies the 2+1 formula or assigns a subtype. FT6.3b decides only the engineering policy/gate; author interpretation remains held.

selection_rule_for_ft6_3b.success-decay-v1: Eligible release policy if it passes the causal and held-out stabilization criteria and, after the exact changed-condition/idle intervention, changes at least one C4-C5 choice relative to success-v1 without violating any invariant.
selection_rule_for_ft6_3b.success-v1: Fallback eligible policy if it passes the causal and held-out stabilization criteria and success-decay-v1 fails a registered invariant or produces no distinct changed-condition response.
selection_rule_for_ft6_3b.null: Selected only if neither non-null policy passes the causal and stabilization criteria; in that case conditioning remains an observation/control and the FT6 behavioral gate is held.
selection_rule_for_ft6_3b.no_tuning: The ordering and criterion are prospective. No rate, threshold, candidate identity, history tag or demand fixture may change after inspecting grid outcomes.

invariants: No evaluator-provided answer, desired route, desired DCNH cell or realized outcome enters candidate construction or choice.
Each chosen behavior is an existing paid native execution; candidate labels, counters and preflight results cannot substitute for the scheduled chosen completion.
The same fixed demand/candidate fixtures are reused across matched policy/history cells. Only the declared history, feedback switch or fixed stable order differs.
Decay changes only bounded scores. It cannot revoke content, access, certificates or H.retained.
A cell that cannot execute its chosen paid behavior remains a preserved failure and contributes no occupancy episode.
Measured occupancy, stabilization and subtype interpretation remain three distinct claims.
gate: Fourteen exact FT6.3a methods pass with zero failures/errors; all 180 primary cells and declared controls have exact identities; every candidate is prospectively preflighted and every chosen behavior binds to actual paid native completion; three policies, five histories, six held-out then six changed demands, exact decay, history-removal, feedback-off and fixed-bias contrasts reconstruct independently; ties and counterexamples persist; all FT6.2-and-earlier method identities remain exact; frozen source is unchanged. Passing records the grid but does not accept the parent FT6.3 gate until FT6.3b.
next: FT6.3a implementation, fixed scenario hashes, bounded grid and private raw evidence, then FT6.3b independent parent-gate decision
theory_boundary: Passing is an engineering causal evaluation. It does not validate psychology, establish the 2+1 formula, elect a subtype, close TD6/TD7 or alter any C/D register.
